text: 1 Foursquare Identity #3 Four Stage Missiology Overview In the 1980s, Foursquare Missions International (United States) developed a missiology in fulfilling the Great Commission of making disciples of all nations. The Four Stage National Development process, which was also visually depicted through a “wheel” (see below), has an end goal of establishing new national churches in nations around the world. “Each stage in the cycle has the goal of reproducing what is infinitely reproducible.” Stage 1--Initiate--to make responsible, reproducing disciples...and begin a local fellowship of believers Stage 2--Nurture--to make responsible, reproducing leaders...of godly character...who mentor...and become leaders of leaders Stage 3--Expand--to make responsible, reproducing congregations who multiply culturally appropriate churches that together become a regional or national church movement Stage 4--Send--to make responsible, reproducing missionary-sending national churches who make disciples of the nations.6 The Four Stage Missiology is examined further in the Disciples of All Nations book by John Amstutz, D.Min. Please read the entire Disciples of All Nations book with this corresponding section. 2 Disciples of All Nations 39 Like an older adult, the church is supportive and sends workers to take the gospel to regions yet untouched with the gospel. The Foursquare cabinet has also approved the fol- lowing amplification of the four-stage national church developmental process, believing it explains and illus- trates how the International Church of the Foursquare Gospel is to continue to fulfill its biblical purpose and historic mission both in North America and around the world. 1 3 Interview Questions • In your own words, please describe each of the four stages and how they promote responsible missional growth. Pastoral Considerations/Application • We want pastors who wholeheartedly value and champion all four stages of missional growth.
